question: A student tracked study hours. Starting with 89 hours, she removed 75 hours already completed (14 hours remaining). She then lost 13 hours to unexpected activities (1 hour). She added 55 new study hours to her schedule (56 hours). She multiplied by 4 for a semester plan (224 hours). She multiplied by 7 for the full academic year (1568 hours). The year was then doubled for a two-year projection. What was the final projected total?

A restaurant tracked items throughout the day. They started with 213 menu items in inventory. Morning added 52 items (265 items). Afternoon delivery added 44 items (309 items). Late afternoon brought 21 items (330 items). Evening suppliers added 71 items (401 items). The total was then multiplied by 8 for weekly inventory planning. A seasonal menu had 156 items separate from daily tracking. What was the planned weekly inventory?

Two gardeners compared yields. One gardener started with 75 tomato plants. By multiplying plantings by 9, she had 675 plants total. Natural losses removed 43 plants (632 plants). She acquired 41 more plants (673 plants). Additional seeds grew into 18 plants (691 plants). A final donation added 61 plants (752 plants). The other gardener had 120 plants this season. What was the final total?

Two investors tracked a fund balance. Starting with 208 dollars, they added 44 dollars in deposits (252 dollars). The fund was multiplied by 7 through interest (1764 dollars). Market losses reduced by 439 dollars (1325 dollars). The balance was multiplied by 6 (7950 dollars). It was then multiplied by 7 again for annual projection. They said the amount would triple by next year. What was the projected annual amount?

Two competitors tracked performance metrics. Starting with 63 points, one competitor lost 10 points early (53 points). Points were then multiplied by 7 through challenges (371 points). They multiplied by 9 through successive achievements (3339 points). They were then multiplied by 5 for ranking purposes (16695 points). A final achievement added 63 points. The rival started with 78 points. What was the final score?

Two colleagues tracked a joint project budget. Starting with 104 dollars, they added 56 dollars (160 dollars). The budget was multiplied by 3 for the full quarter (480 dollars). Major expenses removed 406 dollars (74 dollars). Additional costs reduced by 52 dollars (22 dollars). The remaining amount was doubled for reserves. A separate project had 210 dollars allocated. What was the final budget with reserves?

A production facility tracked material consumption. Starting with 172 kilograms, they consumed 96 kilograms (76 kg remaining). Output was multiplied by 4 through production runs (304 kg). They multiplied by 5 for five facilities (1520 kg). Operations multiplied by 8 across eight shifts (12160 kg). Converting to metric tons, the facility processed about 85.12 metric tons. Final multiplier was 7 for annual estimates. What was the total?

A startup tracked user counts through growth stages. Starting with 231 users, they multiplied by 6 through promotion (1386 users). Growth multiplied by 9 (12474 users). A platform issue lost 12249 users (225 users). Recovery multiplied by 5 (1125 users). Scaling multiplied by 3 (3375 users). A system bug removed 1085 users. How many users remained on the platform?

Two traders compared accounts. One started with 87 dollars. He removed 67 dollars for expenses (20 dollars). His remaining amount was divided equally among 4 investments, with 5 being reinvested (25 dollars reinvested). He withdrew 14 dollars (11 dollars). A final transfer removed 9 dollars. His trading partner had double the starting amount. How many dollars remained?

A music producer started with 106 hours of recordings. They added 18 more hours from recent sessions (124 hours). They then doubled the collection for archival purposes (248 hours). They multiplied by 9 to represent all backup copies (2232 hours). The archive was multiplied by 9 more times for a full preservation set. Half of the collection was on triple backup. What was the total archive size?

A delivery service started with 139 packages. They multiplied through 5 collection rounds (695 packages total). In the first sorting phase, 72 packages were added (767 packages). The second phase added 77 more packages (844 packages). These were then multiplied by 5 to represent all regional routes (4220 packages). Each route then handled one-fifth of the total, consolidating back to the base amount. Converting packages to metric tons, the average weight was triple the starting count. How many packages per route?

A bakery's daily count started at 232 items. In the morning, 58 items were sold (174 items). Mid-morning production multiplied output by 7 (1218 items). By late morning, 20 more items were added from a delivery (1238 items). In the afternoon, a major sale reduced inventory by 880 items (358 items). Late afternoon restocking added 71 items (429 items). By evening, the count was multiplied by 3 for next-day planning. A neighboring bakery had 156 items in their count. What was the evening planning count?

Two gardeners worked together throughout the day. Starting with 169 plants to transplant in the morning, they multiplied their work by 5 (845 plants). By mid-morning, they had added 20 plants (865 plants). At noon, their count doubled as they prepared afternoon sections (1730 plants). Afternoon work added 29 plants (1759 plants). By evening, they were preparing to triple their operation for tomorrow, multiplying by 6 as a projection. What was the evening projection?

Two runners competed in a training program. Starting with 160 kilometers planned, one reduced by 70 kilometers (90 kilometers). They then divided by 2 for two different routes (45 kilometers each). Their first route lost 11 kilometers to terrain issues (34 kilometers). The second route had 31 fewer kilometers. Converting to miles, this represented about 21 miles for the adjusted route. What was the final distance for the first route?

Marcus and Elena tracked points throughout the competition. Starting with 28 points, they multiplied by 5 through initial rounds (140 points). They added 47 bonus points (187 points). They earned 77 more points in challenges (264 points). Their score was then multiplied by 5 (1320 points). The final competition multiplied by 8 for championship scoring. David had earned 95 points separately. What was the championship score?

A factory tracked production through morning, afternoon, and evening shifts. Starting with 117 units, morning shift multiplied by 5 (585 units). By mid-morning, 467 units were sold (118 units). Late morning lost another 47 units (71 units). Afternoon shift multiplied by 7 (497 units). Evening shift multiplied by 3 (1491 units). Night production multiplied by 9. One shift had double the staff of the others. What was the night production?

A delivery company tracked packages through the day. Starting with 155 packages in the morning, they received 49 more (204 packages). Mid-morning delivery added 70 packages (274 packages). By late morning, 160 packages had been delivered (114 packages). Afternoon brought 72 new packages (186 packages). Evening delivery added 13 more (199 packages). Converting total packages to boxes, they needed about 17 shipping boxes. What was the final count?

Two colleagues collaborated on a project. Starting with 102 tasks, they multiplied by 4 to represent all team members' work (408 tasks). They completed 83 tasks early (325 tasks remaining). The remaining workload was multiplied by 6 for the full quarter (1950 tasks). This was multiplied by 9 for annual planning. A competing team had 156 tasks assigned. What was the annual workload?

A store tracked inventory morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 142 items, inventory was doubled in the morning (284 items). Morning sales reduced by 194 items (90 items). Afternoon markdowns reduced by another 89 items (1 item). Evening restock multiplied by 8 (8 items). This was then multiplied by 5 for next week's projection. A clearance sale had 300 items reserved. What was next week's base inventory?

A restaurant tracked customer capacity morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 65 seats available, morning service doubled this (130 seats). By late morning, 78 additional seats were added through patio setup (208 seats). The afternoon service multiplied by 9 to show volume (1872 seats across all services). Evening rush added 55 more capacity measures. Converting to dining parties of 4, this represented about 482 parties. What was the evening capacity?

Two employees tracked hours worked morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 82 hours accumulated, 26 hours went to support (56 hours). Morning projects multiplied by 6 (336 hours). Mid-morning meetings added 20 hours (356 hours). Afternoon meetings removed 104 hours (252 hours). Converting to weeks, this represented about 6.3 work weeks. Marcus had logged 156 hours in the same period. How many hours did the first employee have?

Two teams collaborated morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 37 team members, they added 38 through recruitment (75 members). Morning assignments multiplied by 6 (450 members of projected work). Afternoon expansion multiplied by 3 (1350 units). Team-building activities added 48 people (1398 people). Evening planning added 10 more (1408 people). Sarah led a different team with 96 members. What was the evening total?

A worker starting shift had 69 minutes of tasks. Their workload was divided equally into 3 parts (23 minutes per part). They added 64 minutes of new requests (87 minutes). They then multiplied this for 5 team members' workload (435 minutes total). System delays removed 176 minutes. Converting minutes to hours, they had approximately 4.3 hours of work. How many minutes remained?

A store manager tracked sales throughout the day. Starting with 115 items, 55 were sold by mid-morning (60 items). A restock added 57 items (117 items). By noon, 23 were sold (94 items). Afternoon brought 62 new items (156 items). Late afternoon added 35 more items (191 items). Evening closing removed 74 items from active display. Converting to dozens, this represented about 9.75 dozen items. How many items remained?

A worker tracked tasks through morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 22 tasks, morning work completed 18 (4 tasks). Early afternoon removed another 2 through reassignment (2 tasks). Mid-afternoon brought 45 new tasks (47 tasks). Late afternoon additions brought 62 more (109 tasks). Evening cleanup removed 85 tasks. A colleague had 38 tasks separately. What was the final count?
